Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams have one remaining operational question before we sign the DPA addendum: we need a clear, documented "regional custody handshake" that describes the exact circumstances and controls for any temporary outbound processing (eg. short failover to another region / emergency analytics hop).

Specific asks:
- Maximum transient window you would allow for cross-region processing (hours).
- Which subprocessors would be involved if an EU->US hop happens (and confirmation those subprocessors are on your roster).
- Notification & approval cadence (who we talk to internally at Redwood, SLA for notice).
- Telemetry/audit artifacts we will receive (audit logs, KMS key wrap events).

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our DPA questions and a stub for where we expect evidence. Can your team confirm and, if acceptable, provide a one-page operational playbook we can reference in the DPA?

We are on a tight timeline for a May 3 go/no-go for production. Happy to schedule a 30m call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Security Ops, MedLumen

Hi Elena — appreciate the clear asks. High-level answers below; I also attached a draft one-page playbook and a current subprocessor roster.

Short answers (operational):
- Transient window: default = 0 (no cross-border processing). In emergencies we can allow up to a 48-hour outbound hop for disaster recovery or capacity exhaustion, subject to pre-agreed trigger conditions and monitoring.
- Subprocessors: primary analytics failover path can touch: FastEdge (edge-cache), TelemetryHub (logging), and CloudBridge (ingest). I attach our latest roster with their roles and country of processing.
- Notification & approval: Redwood will send an automated incident notice + an Ops escalation email to medlumen-legal@medlumen.com and your security contact within 30 minutes of the decision to initiate the hop; we will also open a joint incident channel.
- Telemetry/audit: you will receive tokenized audit events (request id, timestamps, source region, target region, node id), plus KMS wrap/unwrap events within the audit bundle. Full request payloads are never exported in cleartext outside the pinned region.

Action items for us:
1) Legal: confirm DPA addendum text accepting the 48-hour emergency hop and specifying notification SLA and approval (DocuSign-ready redlines attached).
2) Ops: Kim / Ben, can you confirm we are comfortable with FastEdge and TelemetryHub for EU->US transient routing and that the KMS key policies meet the acceptance criteria below?

Acceptance criteria (ops):
- KMS: customer-managed key or split-wrap key escrow; key usage logged.
- Cache: prefix caching disabled for pinned payloads during transit window.
- Timebox: automated rollback at 48 hours if not manually renewed.

If that sounds workable I'll get a short one-pager finalized and share the DocuSign link.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_regional_handshake_v2.pdf; subprocessor_roster_20260414.csv
